newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform on rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end weaker, underperform on rate hike.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed sharply weaker in very active trade on Thursday after the Bank of Canada surprised the market by hiking rates for the first time in more than two years, analysts said.

"The market is basically responding to the Bank of Canada's rate hike this morning which wasn't expected. It shored up the currency but put a negative tone on the bond market," said Anita Lauria, an economist with Salomon Brothers.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$1.38 to C$114.89 to yield 6.825 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 16/32 to yield 6.78 percent. The spread between the bonds moved to five basis points from a negative spread of one basis point at Wednesday's close.
Earlier the Bank of Canada raised its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 3.5 percent -- the first move by the bank since it cut rates by 25 basis points on November 8, 1996.

The move brought the bank's target range for the call loan or overnight lending rate to 3.0-3.5 from 2.75-3.25 percent. It was the first time the central bank has raised Canadian short-term interest rates since February, 1995.

Analysts said the rate hike was directly responsible for the Canadian bond market's underperformance relative to the U.S. market. Adding to the Canadian market's woes were portfolio managers' selling of long bonds to lock in strong gains recorded this quarter.

"We saw a lot of guys that had good quarters by being in the long bond the past few months. They're worried about the collapsing market. They're worried about the quarter end performances," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc. "We saw a lot of sellers in the long end."
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$1.02 to C$107.13 to yield 6.263 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which fell 9/32 to yield 6.49 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 23 basis points from 30 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.18 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.12 percent.
